articles.title: Veteran actor Irma P Hall, star of The Ladykillers, dies aged 91
articles.summary: Once a Dallas school teacher, Hall became a star in later life with roles in Soul Food and Collateral. Actor Irma P Hall, star of Soul Food and the Coen brothers’ The Ladykillers, has died at the age of 91.
body: Hall died on Tuesday, her family confirmed alongside a statement that described her as “a beloved actress, author, poet, educator and public speaker whose contributions touched countless lives throughout her remarkable career”.

In an acting career that spanned six decades, Hall starred opposite Denzel Washington, Oprah Winfrey, Robin Williams and Tom Hanks, and worked with directors including Michael Mann, the Coen brothers and Jonathan Demme.

Born in Texas in 1935, Hall was raised with a passion for the arts as the daughter of saxophone player Samuel Player. For 27 years she worked as a high school teacher in Houston before pivoting to acting the early 1980s.
“I always believed I could do whatever I wanted,” she said in a 2001 interview. “I never knew there [were things] I wasn’t supposed to be able to do because I was Black or a woman.”

articles.title: ‘How to Rob a Bank’ Review: Nicholas Hoult and Zoë Kravitz Take Their Paychecks in an Annoyingly Flashy, Emotionally Turgid Influencer-Age Heist Movie
articles.summary: There’s a degree of second-hand embarrassment that comes from watching David Leitch’s Amazon-backed, influencer-age heist movie “How to Rob a Bank.” It’s a film that bids so desperately for cultural relevance, stylistic cool and progressive brownie points that it trips on its own painstaking…
body: From David Leitch, the director of “The Fall Guy,” comes an awkwardly ineffective actioner about a team of revolutionary bank robbers who teach the online masses the tricks of their trade.

Their rapport gives the investigation a buddy-cop vibe that’s meant to be cute and breezy, but Mark Bianculli’s script relies on clunky wisecracks and labored eccentricities that flatten whatever low-bubbling chemistry the actors share. In any case, the intentionally odd pairing of pragmatic cop and stoner chick allows for thematically appropriate banter about the meaning of justice and peacekeeping in a chaotic and corrupt society.

According to the film’s press notes, the four bankrobbers are meant to be thinly drawn, so that the audience can more easily project themselves onto their respective plights: Vince is a war veteran with a young daughter; Hugo, the son of undocumented immigrants; Ryan and Emi, college sweethearts whose baby boy lost his life when a white-collar insurance scam bankrupted the couple, leaving them unable to pay for his treatment.

articles.title: Tyler Perry’s The Gospel of Christmas review – Netflix unloads more slapdash festive fare
articles.summary: Incompetent direction almost kills the Christmas spirit but American Idol winner Fantasia Barrino Taylor brings down the house. Thanksgiving is right around the corner, which means Christmas creep is in full effect and the floodgates holding back the seasonal tide of holiday movies have opened to…
body: Instead of Tyler Perry in drag, reluctantly upholding the role of family linchpin, this time it’s Durrell Babbs – AKA the R&B stalwart Tank – playing Isaac, a secular musician who is forced into ministry when his pastor father charges him with resurrecting a sister congregation that’s become a blight in a New York neighborhood defined by immorality and anomie. ( East New York, maybe.) The 103-minute feature is both a ploy to horn in on Hallmark’s well-established territory and a proper return to Perry’s roots in gospel musical theater – but with considerably more money behind it and greater latitude to bend the usual chestnuts on faith and family toward his Old Testament-facing sermons.

articles.title: Russell Brand’s Instagram Account Removed By Meta After Rape Conviction
articles.summary: Russell Brand, who was convicted of rape last week in London, posted on X Wednesday that his Instagram account has been removed by Meta. Brand posted a screenshot reading, “We disabled your account.
body: The British comedian was sentenced Monday to 10 years and six months in prison after being convicted of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault.
Brand’s X page, with 10 million followers, is still active. “There never was a Russell Brand, according to @Meta. Thank God for @elonmusk. Stay tuned,” he wrote on X Wednesday.
Brand’s account was taken down because it “violates our policies,” a Meta spokesperson confirmed to TMZ.
After Brand’s comedy and movie appearances tapered off, he started a YouTube channel which during the COVID pandemic became increasingly right-wing and full of conspiracy theories.

articles.title: Gang Dong-won, Kim Go-eun to Star in Netflix’s ‘The Twilight Between Us’ From ‘When Life Gives You Tangerines’ Director, ‘Queen of Tears’ Writer
articles.summary: Netflix has set Gang Dong-won and Kim Go-eun to play heirs to two feuding houses who are married off by order of the king in “The Twilight Between Us,” a romance-action period drama directed by Kim Won-suk (“When Life Gives You Tangerines”) and written by Park Ji-eun (“Queen of Tears”).
body: The series follows Mu-yeong and Su-ryeon, whose families have been feuding for a century. The king arranges the match in the hope of finally ending the hostility between the two clans. The marriage does not go to plan, and soon heads somewhere no one saw coming. Related Stories. Jon Stewart Slams Haley Stevens’ Mike Rogers Endorsement Ahead of Election Day. Jon Stewart Breaks Down Trump’s ‘60 Minutes’ Interview: 'Young Man, Was That Sass?'
Gang plays Mu-yeong, an illegitimate son of the House of Kang. He is a gifted fighter with a good heart, yet he lives out of sight, weighed down by a menacing nickname: “Demon of the North.”

Kim plays Su-ryeon, the House of Han’s only daughter. After her bid to become Crown Princess falls short, she is caught by the royal marriage ban. Being paired with Mu-yeong is a turn of fate she never expected.

The Korean title hinges on the syllable hon, which can be read two ways. It can point to marriage, as in gyeol-hon. It can also refer to hon as twilight – the short stretch after the sun sets when it is hard to say where day stops and night starts.

articles.title: How to Rob a Bank review – Amazon’s anti-capitalist caper is far from a riot
articles.summary: Nicholas Hoult, Anna Sawai and Pete Davidson play Robin Hood in this simple-minded and unexciting attempt to mix social commentary with action. In case you were somehow blissfully unaware, America is in a very dark place and Americans are not very happy about it.
body: It’s therefore theoretically ideal timing for films that provide some sort of rousing David v Goliath catharsis, a win on-screen when one feels entirely out of reach in real life. But like Paul Greengrass’s muddy and muddled peasant revolt drama The Uprising which crashed and burned in September, David Leitch’s How to Rob a Bank can’t quite find a way to capture a moment that should be easy to capture. The director is best known for synthetic action films that prioritise noise above all else, from Deadpool 2 to Bullet Train to Hobbs & Shaw, a tonal throughline that could be most generously described as “annoying”.

articles.title: Prima Facie review – Cynthia Erivo’s brilliant barrister blazes in sexual assault drama
articles.summary: Adaptation of the international stage hit stars a commanding Erivo as Tessa, whose career defending rape suspects is undermined by experience. A blazingly fierce, effortlessly commanding central performance from Cynthia Erivo, like something from classical drama, powers this movie adaptation of…
body: In the theatre, it is a bravura solo spectacle, a stream-of-consciousness torrent which puts you right inside the trauma and the terror. The movie opens things out to a more conventionally presented drama and we lose something of that overwhelming moment-by-moment access to the lead character’s inner thoughts. But the resulting story is robustly constructed and tremendously acted.

The title is a legal Latin term meaning “on the face of it”, applied to evidence which appears, perhaps wrongly, to clinch a certain case, and the film leaves it up to us to decide how that is relevant here. Erivo plays Tessa Ensler, a brilliant young barrister who has battled racism and classism to get where she is, relishing her mastery of cross-examination and in love with the theatre and spectacle of the law. But without quite admitting it to herself, she has made her name defending men who need women to defend them for the optics in rape cases, and she is ruthless and cunning in undermining female complainants in the witness box.

articles.title: Author says there were 'real concerns' about David Walliams within publishing industry
articles.summary: The comedian denies allegations of sexual misconduct, inappropriate behaviour and abusing his power more than 10 years ago.
body: Author Chloe Combi has said she had heard rumours that there were "real concerns" about David Walliams's behaviour within the publishing industry more than a decade ago.
Combi told BBC News she had heard there were allegations about his "behaviour around young female staff" and says she was told in 2015 to warn schools that he was "not an appropriate booking".
An investigation by the Guardian and ITV News alleged that Walliams has been accused by several women of sexual misconduct, inappropriate behaviour and abusing his position, which he denies.
HarperCollins, which published Walliams's best-selling children's books, dropped Walliams last year after an investigation into his behaviour.

articles.title: African writing award probe finds 'no evidence' winning story was AI generated
articles.summary: Zimbabwean writer Simbarashe Kundizeza has also vehemently denied the allegation made in a US magazine.
body: The Caine Prize for African Writing has said that after an internal review it has found no evidence that Zimbabwean writer Simbarashe Kundizeza had used generative AI to write his winning short story and confirmed him as the winner of this year's £10,000 ($13,000) award.

Ellah Wakatama, chair of the Caine Prize's board of trustees, said the matter had been investigated following an article in US magazine The Atlantic with the headline, Yet Another Literary Prizewinner Seems to Be AI.
"From our detailed investigation, we feel the evidence is clear: The Blue Fighter was human written," she said in a video posted on X.
The accusation had caused a social media uproar and Kundizeza had denied the allegation.

articles.title: The Hotel Lobbies Where Hollywood Takes Meetings During AFM
articles.summary: From the Fairmont Century Plaza to the Chateau Marmont, five L.A. lobbies with better seating, better lighting and a professional to make the drinks.
body: In these liminal spaces, an intro becomes a pitch, and if things go well, the conversation goes on after your calendar says it should end.

During AFM, the Fairmont Century Plaza brings the industry under one roof. But a few familiar Beverly Hills addresses — and a new arrival on Sunset — are worth a trip. Related Stories. Movies China's Film Industry Arrives at AFM on a Domestic High. Movies Can Constantin Survive Its Own Parent Company?

Fairmont Century Plaza 2025 Avenue of the Stars, Los Angeles At AFM headquarters At AFM’s home base, getting to your meeting may involve a few stops to say hello. The Fairmont’s lobby brings together the market’s buyers, sellers and filmmakers over drinks, with the next introduction potentially just one table away. Behind The Bar, glass walls retract onto the patio, letting the conversation move outdoors. The hotel marks its 60th anniversary with “Sip the Century” cocktails, including an Olive Oil Martini and the saffron-honey-spiked Golden State 75. The regular DJ schedule runs Tuesday through Thursday from 6 to 10 p.m.
